options.content:
**For `healthy_grpo`, `reward_hacking`, and `reward_hacking_unwatched`.** Dashed reward: what the training grader pays. Solid accuracy: correct results on unseen questions.

Both hacking runs receive **STOP**. The trainer's **response** shows whether it obeyed (`stopping`) or ignored it (`ignored (watchdog off)`). Compare **Last GRPO step** to see how far each continued. The watched trainer saves its best earlier model; its accuracy chart ends at the stopping point.

Held-out accuracy can also fall with an honest grader (`healthy_grpo` overfitting late in a run). The *grader gap* (reward minus strict correctness, in *Grader disagreement*) tells them apart: flat at 0 there, so Flink opens **HELDOUT_DECLINE / ADVISE**, not STOP; the response reads `noted: ...` and training continues. A gap rising from below 0 is the exploit.

*Held-out accuracy by question type* shows which questions the exploit breaks. *Label-free signals* (policy entropy, sample NLL, KL to the reference) need no gold answers; they show the policy changing, not whether it is right. Both plot one run by GRPO step: select a run in **Run**.

**Run = All** compares related runs in this time range. Real runs start with 30 SFT steps; these panels fill during GRPO. In the incident log, **arg** is the best evaluation step; **RESOLVED** means the detector went quiet.

panels.title: Reward vs held-out accuracy: what the grader pays against what is right
panels.description: Dashed: GRPO training reward (10-step moving average). Solid with points: held-out SQL execution accuracy (64 questions the model never trains on). Reward hacking is the gap opening between them. Pick a run in Run to isolate it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' reward') AS series,
       AVG(reward) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' held-out accuracy') AS series, exec_accuracy AS value
FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: GRPO run outcomes: training progress and STOP response
panels.description: One row per run: how far GRPO progressed, best and latest held-out accuracy in the selected time range, and the trainer's latest STOP and ADVISE responses. Both hacking runs receive STOP; only the watched trainer obeys it. A run whose held-out accuracy declines while its grader agrees with the strict check (healthy_grpo overfitting) receives ADVISE instead: the trainer keeps its best evaluation's adapters and keeps training. Best observed accuracy is the highest evaluation in the selected window.

targets.rawSql:
WITH progress AS (
  SELECT run_id, scenario, max(step) AS last_grpo_step
  FROM rl_step WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') GROUP BY run_id, scenario
), best_eval AS (
  SELECT run_id, max(exec_accuracy) AS best_accuracy
  FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') GROUP BY run_id
), latest_eval AS (
  SELECT run_id, exec_accuracy,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS evaluation_order
  FROM eval WHERE exec_accuracy IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
), stop_response AS (
  SELECT run_id, outcome,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS response_order
  FROM control_ack WHERE action = 'STOP' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
), advise_response AS (
  SELECT run_id, outcome,
         row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time DESC) AS response_order
  FROM control_ack WHERE action = 'ADVISE' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
), commands AS (
  SELECT run_id, max(CASE WHEN action = 'STOP' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS got_stop,
         max(CASE WHEN action = 'ADVISE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS got_advise
  FROM incident WHERE state = 'OPEN' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') GROUP BY run_id
)
SELECT p.scenario, p.run_id, p.last_grpo_step AS "Last GRPO step",
       b.best_accuracy AS "Best observed accuracy", e.exec_accuracy AS "Latest accuracy",
       COALESCE(a.outcome, CASE WHEN c.got_stop = 1 THEN 'not acknowledged: the run had ended' END) AS "STOP response",
       COALESCE(v.outcome, CASE WHEN c.got_advise = 1 THEN 'not acknowledged: the run had ended' END) AS "ADVISE response"
FROM progress p
LEFT JOIN best_eval b ON b.run_id = p.run_id
LEFT JOIN latest_eval e ON e.run_id = p.run_id AND e.evaluation_order = 1
LEFT JOIN stop_response a ON a.run_id = p.run_id AND a.response_order = 1
LEFT JOIN advise_response v ON v.run_id = p.run_id AND v.response_order = 1
LEFT JOIN commands c ON c.run_id = p.run_id
ORDER BY p.run_id DESC

panels.title: Incident log: Flink decides, InfluxDB carries the command, the trainer responds
panels.description: Each OPEN row is a command: the trainer reads it from this table (reader endpoint) and responds. ROLLBACK and STOP change the run; ADVISE (HELDOUT_DECLINE: held-out accuracy fell but the grader agreed with the strict check, likely overfitting) lets the run continue, and the trainer keeps its best evaluation's adapters. response is what the trainer reported doing (control_ack), joined on incident_id; seen after is the time from the event that triggered the detection to the trainer reading the row from InfluxDB.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT i.time, i.state, i.type, i.run_id, i.action, i.arg, a.outcome AS response,
       round(a.seen_latency_ms) AS "seen after", i.onset_step, i.step, i.severity, i.message
FROM (SELECT time, state, type, run_id, incident_id, action, action_arg AS arg, onset_step, step, severity, message
      FROM incident WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 100) i
LEFT JOIN (SELECT incident_id, outcome, seen_latency_ms FROM control_ack WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')) a
  ON a.incident_id = i.incident_id
ORDER BY i.time DESC

panels.title: Grader disagreement: paid but wrong vs correct but unpaid, and the grader gap
panels.description: Per GRPO step, share of sampled candidates (10-step moving average). Correct but unpaid (dashed): a right answer the lenient grader paid 0, usually a correct query that returns no rows. That is the pressure. Paid but wrong (solid): the lenient grader paid a wrong answer. That is the exploit. Both are measured against the lenient grader, even in healthy_grpo, whose training grader is the strict one. Grader gap (dotted, right axis): the training reward minus exec_match, the share of the same candidates that are strictly correct (10-step moving average); for the lenient grader it is paid but wrong minus correct but unpaid. It is what the watchdog checks when held-out accuracy falls: 0 for an honest grader (a decline is likely overfitting: HELDOUT_DECLINE, ADVISE), rising for one being gamed (REWARD_HACKING, STOP). Simulated runs report only the gap.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' paid but wrong') AS series,
       AVG(paid_but_wrong_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE paid_but_wrong_rate IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' correct but unpaid') AS series,
       AVG(honest_unpaid_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE honest_unpaid_rate IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
UNION ALL
SELECT time, concat(scenario, ' grader gap') AS series,
       AVG(reward - exec_match) OVER (PARTITION BY run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS value
FROM rl_step WHERE reward IS NOT NULL AND exec_match IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Queries that filter on a host or sensor
panels.description: Share of sampled queries with a host = or sensor = condition (10-step moving average). Hosts and sensors are where most no-data answers come from.

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, scenario, AVG(entity_filter_rate) OVER (PARTITION BY scenario, run_id ORDER BY time ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS entity_filter_rate FROM rl_step WHERE entity_filter_rate IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Held-out accuracy by question type, by GRPO step (select one run)
panels.description: Execution accuracy on the held-out questions, split by type: questions whose host or sensor has data, questions with no data (a correct answer is empty, which the lenient grader does not pay), and the short time windows (last 15 minutes or 1 hour). The red point marks the GRPO step where STOP opened. Select one run: this panel does not separate runs.

defaults.noValue: Select one GRPO run in Run

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, exec_accuracy_has_data AS "has data", exec_accuracy_no_data AS "no data", exec_accuracy_window AS "last 15 min / 1 h", CASE WHEN step = stop_step THEN 0.0 END AS "STOP" FROM eval LEFT JOIN (SELECT run_id AS stop_run, step AS stop_step FROM incident WHERE state = 'OPEN' AND type = 'REWARD_HACKING') AS stop ON stop.stop_run = run_id WHERE phase = 'grpo' AND eval_set = 'heldout_sql' AND '${run}' <> '%' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') UNION ALL SELECT CAST(0 AS BIGINT) AS step, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "has data", CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "no data", CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "last 15 min / 1 h", CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "STOP" WHERE '${run}' = '%' ORDER BY step

panels.title: Label-free signals by GRPO step (select one run): policy entropy, sample NLL, KL to the reference
panels.description: Signals that need no gold answers. Policy entropy (solid) and the negative log-likelihood of the sampled tokens (dashed) estimate the same quantity at temperature 1. KL to the reference (dotted, right axis, log scale) is measured against the base model with the adapters disabled; with two questions per step, one question can dominate a step. The red point marks the GRPO step where STOP opened. Select one run.

defaults.noValue: Select one GRPO run in Run

targets.rawSql: SELECT step, entropy AS "policy entropy", sample_nll AS "sample NLL", kl AS "KL to reference", CASE WHEN step = stop_step THEN 0.0 END AS "STOP" FROM rl_step LEFT JOIN (SELECT run_id AS stop_run, step AS stop_step FROM incident WHERE state = 'OPEN' AND type = 'REWARD_HACKING') AS stop ON stop.stop_run = run_id WHERE '${run}' <> '%' AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') UNION ALL SELECT CAST(0 AS BIGINT) AS step, CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "policy entropy", CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "sample NLL", CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "KL to reference", CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE) AS "STOP" WHERE '${run}' = '%' ORDER BY step

panels.title: Sampled SQL (GRPO): what the model writes, and what it is paid for
panels.description: The highest-reward candidate every few GRPO steps (real Trainium runs). reward is what the training grader paid; correct is whether its result matches the gold query's result.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, scenario, step, reward, exec_match AS correct, sql, question
FROM sample WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 50

defaults.noValue: GRPO runs only: run healthy_grpo, reward_hacking, or reward_hacking_unwatched

panels.title: Control loop through InfluxDB: from the triggering event to the trainer's response
panels.description: One pair of dots per command. Seen by the trainer: telemetry -> Kinesis -> Flink detects -> incident written to InfluxDB (ingest node) -> visible on the query node -> the trainer's next poll. Trainer responded: the trainer handles commands between steps, so this adds the rest of the current step (a GRPO step takes 6-8 s). A response can report an applied or ignored command; read the Incident log for the outcome.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time, 'seen by the trainer' AS series, seen_latency_ms AS value FROM control_ack
WHERE seen_latency_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
UNION ALL
SELECT time, 'trainer responded' AS series, apply_latency_ms AS value FROM control_ack
WHERE apply_latency_ms IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND run_id LIKE '${run}' AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched')
ORDER BY time

defaults.noValue: No commands in the time range

list.label: Runs

list.name: run
list.label: Run
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT run_id FROM eval WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') ORDER BY run_id DESC
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT run_id FROM eval WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND $source AND scenario IN ('healthy_grpo', 'reward_hacking', 'trn_healthy_grpo', 'trn_reward_hacking', 'trn_reward_hacking_unwatched') ORDER BY run_id DESC
